app.angNodeNote: Node.js ranges come from angular.dev's official compatibility table for each major, not from this app's own toolchain.
app.angVersionsIntro: Every Angular major from 14 to 22 is a real generation target: its own builder, bootstrap strategy, SSR package and capability set. Only Angular 22 has an executed build behind it — this repository is one. Older majors are modeled from Angular's published compatibility data, not run here.
app.archCustomHelp: Custom lets you name every bucket yourself — core, shared, layout, and the folder that groups your domains or features — instead of accepting one of the other three fixed contracts. Reach for it when your team already has a folder convention and the generator should follow it rather than the other way round.
app.archDddHelp: Domain-driven groups code by what it means to the business, not by its technical type. Each domain owns its full stack — model, use case, repository, component — so a change to one domain rarely touches another. Best for a project with several distinct areas that will each keep growing.
app.archFeatureHelp: Feature-based gives every feature its own self-contained folder — pages, components, services and models together — without the four-layer split DDD asks for. Best when features are the natural unit of the product and rarely share deep logic with one another.
app.archSimpleHelp: Simple keeps everything in one flat app folder — pages, components, services, models — with no per-slice grouping at all. Best for a small, focused project where a folder-per-domain or folder-per-feature split would be overhead, not structure.
app.caRespD: Shared breakpoints, used by every component.
app.caRtlD: Direction-aware helpers plus font overrides for RTL.
app.caTokensD: Radius, spacing and breakpoint maps in _tokens.scss.
app.caVarsD: Every colour is a custom property, scoped per theme.
app.cjkNote: Chinese uses a system font stack. Self-hosting a full CJK face would break the source project's performance budget.
app.csrJsonLdWarn: With browser-only rendering, structured data is written after hydration and some crawlers will not see it. Allowed, but worth a decision before you ship.
app.cssArchD: These come with the architecture template. They are not separate switches.
app.custNotAvail: Copying a template requires a modern (standalone-components) Angular version.
app.datePickerD: A popover calendar picker with keyboard support — generator-authored, since no source-project template exists for this one.
app.dddD: core / domains / shared / layout, with a four-layer slice per domain.
app.coreAuthD: Login/logout, a token-aware interceptor and an auth guard. Requires Storage.
app.coreAuthzD: Role checks, a role guard and a structural directive. Requires Authentication.
app.coreCapD: Each one resolves to a real, generated implementation — the same template system as Toast, Modal and Date picker above.
app.coreErrD: A global ErrorHandler plus HTTP error mapping, normalized to one AppError shape.
app.coreHttpD: A typed HttpClient wrapper with centralized error normalization. Requires Error handling.
app.coreRoutingD: Typed path building and query-param helpers.
app.coreStoreD: SSR-safe localStorage + cookie persistence, prefixed per project.
app.dualModeD: The source project ships both, switchable at runtime.
app.exDomainD: Writes one complete, working {{group}} slice, so the pattern is visible in the code instead of only in the README.
app.exDomainOff: Only the base structure is written, without an example {{group}}.
